newsitem.title: CANADA: Small Canada oil firm signs huge Yemen land deal.
newsitem.headline: Small Canada oil firm signs huge Yemen land deal.

text.p: A little-known Canadian oil company was in the midst of forging final agreements on Thursday to explore what it believes is the largest oil concession ever awarded a foreign firm in Yemen.

Calgary-based Calvalley Petroleum Inc, a 28-employee firm listed on the Montreal Exchange, signed memoranda of understanding with Yemen to explore two sectors totalling 15,000 square km, Ed Shimoon, the company's president, told Reuters in an interview.
"We are meeting with our representatives from the Middle East -- they are coming to Calgary on Monday and we'll be finalizing some additional agreements with them pertaining to Yemen," Shimoon said.
The acreage covered by the MOUs includes sector nine between Yemen's Shabwa and Hadramout provinces and sector 39 in Mahra province.
Sector nine is located between a producing field operated by Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, one of Yemen's most prominent foreign investors, and another operated by France's Total SA.

Sector 39 is located on once-disputed land on the Yemen-Oman border, which is now under Yemeni control. Phillips Petroleum operates an exploration concession in Oman, across the border from the Calvalley lands, Shimoon said.
The deal's final agreement, which was to include fiscal terms with the government, was expected to be signed next week, he said.
Shimoon said his firm, which began public trading in July, had already received expressions of interest from international oil firms to form a joint venture for the concession.
The company, howver, had no immediate plans to form a consortium, he said.
The blocks currently produce no oil, although seismic data covering some of the acreage exists, he said. The agreement would allow Calvalley to explore on the lands for a six-year term.
Shimoon, an engineer by trade who established the company under the name ORI Energy, a private firm, in 1989, said Callvalley was also negotiating other expoloration deals in the Middle East.
Last week, Yemen also signed exploration memoranda of understanding with Kerr-McGee Corp.
Calvalley Petroleum shares were halted at C$2 on Thursday.
